concepts.title: Alvars and Nayanars of Tamilakam
concepts.section: The Alvars and Nayanars of Tamil Nadu
concepts.definition: From about the sixth century, Alvar devotees of Vishnu and Nayanar saints of Shiva travelled singing Tamil hymns, criticised caste and ritualism, and included women like Andal and Karaikkal Ammaiyar; their songs were later compiled in the Divya Prabandham and Tevaram and temple-building institutionalised their cults.
concepts.key_idea: Tamil bhakti made devotion a public, sung and caste-questioning practice, later housed in grand temples.

concepts.title: Philosophy and Virashaiva Tradition
concepts.definition: Shankara taught advaita, the doctrine of the oneness of the individual soul and the supreme god, while Ramanuja's vishishtadvaita urged devotion to Vishnu as the path; in twelfth-century Karnataka Basavanna's Virashaiva movement rejected temple worship and caste, questioning rebirth theory.
concepts.key_idea: Philosophical schools and populist movements both claimed the true path, changing how devotion and doctrine met.
concepts.textbook_ref: lehs202.txt Shankara, Ramanuja and Basavanna sections

solution_steps.explain: advaita asserts oneness; vishishtadvaita keeps qualified difference with devotion
vachanas attacked temples, caste and rebirth doctrine
philosophy spoke in Sanskrit academies, vachanas in working people's Kannada

concepts.title: Sufi Silsilas and the Chishti Order
concepts.section: Growth of Sufism and the Chishtis in the Subcontinent
concepts.definition: Sufis organised into silsilas - chains of spiritual descent - centred on khanqahs where shaikhs trained disciples; the Chishti silsila of Moinuddin Chishti at Ajmer won pan-Indian fame through qawwali singing, langar hospitality and the cult of ziyarat at dargahs, attracting kings and commoners.
concepts.key_idea: The Chishti khanqah blended music, food and discipline so effectively that its dargah remains a living pilgrimage.

concepts.title: Kabir, Guru Nanak and Vernacular Devotion
concepts.section: New Devotional Paths: Kabir, Guru Nanak and Mirabai
concepts.definition: Kabir's poetry in mixed vernaculars mocked both Hindu and Muslim orthodoxy in favour of a formless divine; Guru Nanak preached nam, dan and isnan, and his hymns were collected in the Guru Granth Sahib; Mirabai defied royal household norms for devotion to Krishna.
concepts.key_idea: Vernacular devotion made faith portable: sung poems crossed sects, and collections like the Granth built new communities.
